title: Land Cruiser FJ62
verdict: The FJ62 is where the Land Cruiser put on a collared shirt: fuel injection, an automatic, square headlights and power everything, all on the same leaf-sprung frame that crossed the Outback. It is the easiest old Cruiser to drive every day, and one of the hardest to find without rust.

paragraphs: The FJ62 is the last and most civilized of the 60 Series, and in America it marked the point where the Land Cruiser started to become a luxury vehicle. Hagerty says it brought two Land Cruiser firsts to the US: electronic fuel injection, on the 4.0-liter 3F-E six, and an automatic transmission. Toyota's own history picks out the new dash, the upgraded interior and the rectangular headlamps that make a 1988 easy to spot. Underneath, it's still a ladder-frame, leaf-sprung, solid-axle truck, much like the [[land-cruiser/fj60|FJ60]] it replaced.

story.heading: BUILT FOR JAPAN, SOLD TO AMERICA
paragraphs: The FJ62 started at home. Wikipedia dates the 3F-E injected engine to 1987, when the FJ62G VX allowed the Land Cruiser to be registered in Japan as a passenger vehicle rather than a commercial one. That meant comfort features: Flexmotor lists power windows and locks among the new options. The US got the FJ62 for the 1988 model year, and for American buyers it was a noticeably more comfortable, easier-driving truck than the FJ60.

The 3F-E made 155 hp at 4,000 rpm and 220 lb-ft at 3,000 rpm, against the FJ60's carbureted 135 hp and 210 lb-ft. It drove through Toyota's A440F four-speed automatic, the only US transmission, which Wikipedia describes as the first automatic in a Japanese four-wheel drive. Corsetti Cruisers lists the curb weight at 4,480 lb, 234 lb more than an FJ60, and fuel economy of 12 mpg city and 19 highway, one better than the carbureted truck.

story.heading: STILL A TRUCK UNDERNEATH
paragraphs: For all the velour and power windows, the FJ62 kept the 60 Series hardware: leaf springs, a closed-knuckle Birfield front axle and a two-speed, part-time transfer case. That makes it as capable in the dirt as an FJ60 and as simple to work on, with many parts shared across the 40, 55 and 60 Series. Toyota UK says push-button electro-pneumatic four-wheel-drive engagement replaced manual levers on the 60 from August 1986, so FJ62 owners should check that the system engages cleanly.

The 3F-E has its own following. IH8MUD members note it was used only in the FJ62 and the 1991–92 [[land-cruiser/80-series|FJ80]], and consider a well-kept example with 159,000 miles to have plenty of life left. The common gripes are the ones you'd expect on a 35-year-old truck: oil leaks, vacuum leaks that cause a rough idle, tired A/C and, above all, rust. As one member put it, 'any '88 Cruiser is going to leak some oil, from somewhere.'

story.heading: THE END OF THE LEAF-SPRING WAGON
paragraphs: Japanese production of the 60 Series ended around the turn of 1990; Toyota UK puts the total at 406,700. Venezuela kept building 60s for its own market until 1992, and Wikipedia says the last carbureted 3F FJ62 rolled out of the Cumaná plant that year. In the US the FJ62 handed over to the [[land-cruiser/80-series|80 Series]] for 1991, which kept the 3F-E and automatic for two years but switched to coil springs and full-time four-wheel drive.

That makes the FJ62 the last leaf-sprung Land Cruiser wagon sold in America, and the most comfortable vintage Cruiser you can drive every day. Hagerty calls the round-headlight FJ60 the bigger collector's prize and puts 60 Series median quotes around $18,500, but the FJ62's fuel injection and automatic make it the easier truck to live with. Restomod shops such as Corsetti Cruisers build both.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · WANT THREE PEDALS?
callout.title: Converting an FJ62 to a manual
paragraphs: US FJ62s only came with the A440F automatic, so some owners swap in the H55F five-speed used in other markets. IH8MUD's swap guide lists what it takes: a manual bellhousing, flywheel and clutch kit, crossmember and floor-cover modifications, transfer-case shift linkage, driveshaft changes, a clutch pedal, master and slave cylinders with hard line and hose, and minor wiring changes.
It's a big job, but the H55F's 0.845:1 fifth and deeper first suit both highway driving and trail work.

engineering_intro: The FJ62 is a 60 Series chassis with a modernized powertrain: the fuel-injected 3F-E four-liter six and an A440F four-speed automatic feeding a two-speed, part-time transfer case. Suspension is still leaf springs on solid axles, with the closed-knuckle Birfield front axle shared with the [[land-cruiser/fj60|FJ60]] and late [[land-cruiser/fj40|FJ40]].

engineering.note: Same body structure as the FJ60, with a new nose and square headlights.

engineering.v: Solid axles, leaf springs front and rear
engineering.note: Old Man Emu kits for 4/1985–1/1990 trucks fit the FJ62.
Push-button electro-pneumatic engagement on 60s from August 1986, per Toyota UK.
155 hp @ 4,000 rpm, 220 lb-ft @ 3,000 rpm. Also used in the 1991–92 FJ80.
The only US transmission; H55F manual swaps are possible but involved.

engineering.v: Power-assisted ventilated front discs, rear drums

generations_table.note: A440F automatic only, square headlights, new dash.
Built at Cumaná for the local market after Japanese production ended.
The diesel 60 the US never got.
The successor carried the 3F-E over for two years.

buying_checks.head: Rear frame rails
buying_checks.body: Corsetti says this is the most important check on any 60: drop the spare if necessary and inspect the rear frame rails. Rusted through means walk away.

buying_checks.head: The usual 60 rust spots
buying_checks.body: Windshield gasket corners, roof drip rails, tailgate hinge areas, inner and outer rear wheel wells, front fenders and rockers. Trucks from salted-road states rust fast; a magnet finds filler around the wheel wells and tailgate.

buying_checks.head: Find the oil leak
buying_checks.body: Most will have one. Before blaming the rear main seal, IH8MUD members suggest checking that the oil pan bolts are torqued to spec and that the valve cover gasket isn't the real culprit.

buying_checks.head: Rough idle
buying_checks.body: Usually a tune-up item or a vacuum leak rather than anything serious, but it's a useful bargaining point.

buying_checks.head: Test the A/C and the 4WD
buying_checks.body: Check that the A/C compressor engages; it may just need a recharge. Engage four-wheel drive and low range on a loose surface and make sure the push-button system works.

buying_checks.head: Knuckles and steering
buying_checks.body: Look for sludge at the front knuckles, and drive it to check for wobble or wander, especially on a lifted truck.

buying_checks.head: Power-steering leaks
buying_checks.body: A wet, shiny driver's-side axle and spring usually means the power-steering box or pump is leaking.

buying_checks.head: Ask about the transfer case
buying_checks.body: IH8MUD members treated a transfer-case rebuild at 74,000 miles as a red flag on one truck. Ask why any major driveline work was done.

repairs.title: Chase down a rough idle
repairs.symptoms: Rough or hunting idle, hesitation, or a hiss under the hood.
repairs.fix: Start with a tune-up: plugs, cap, rotor and wires. Then check every vacuum hose, since IH8MUD members point to vacuum leaks as the most likely cause on the 3F-E. Replace hard or cracked hoses rather than patching them, and recheck the idle once warm. Trucks over 200,000 miles will probably need a full set of vacuum hoses.
repairs.tools: Vacuum gauge · smoke tester or carb cleaner spray · vacuum diagram · hose and clamps

repairs.title: Diagnose oil leaks before pulling the transmission
repairs.cost: Gaskets; a rear main seal job is far more
repairs.symptoms: Oil drips at the bellhousing or under the engine.
repairs.fix: Clean the engine, then drive and look again. IH8MUD members point out that a leak near the rear main is often just oil pan bolts not tightened to spec, or a valve cover gasket running down the back of the block. Torque the pan bolts and replace the valve cover gasket before committing to a rear main seal, which means removing the transmission.
repairs.tools: Degreaser · torque wrench · valve cover gasket · UV dye (optional)

repairs.title: Front knuckle rebuild
repairs.symptoms: Grease sludge leaking from the steering knuckles.
repairs.fix: Pull the hub, spindle and Birfield, remove the knuckle caps and bearings, replace the inner axle seal, knuckle bearings and wiper seals, then repack and reassemble. Top shims set knuckle-bearing preload; follow the factory service manual for the spec.
repairs.tools: Spring scale · seal driver · Cruiser Corps kit 595-102 or 514-109 (to 1/1990) · knuckle shim and gasket kit 595-101 · moly grease

parts.name: Knuckle rebuild kit, 9/1975–12/1989 4x/5x/6x/7x disc axle (FA7590) — check VIN on 1990 trucks

repairs.title: Two-inch lift with steering damper
repairs.cost: Old Man Emu kits about $2,400 (Cruiser Corps)
repairs.symptoms: Sagging springs, worn shocks, or front-end shake after bumps.
repairs.fix: Old Man Emu's FJ60/FJ62 kits for 4/1985–1/1990 trucks include springs, Nitrocharger shocks, greaseable shackles and pins, spring bushings, U-bolts and an OMESD24 steering damper. Choose light, medium or heavy load springs for how the truck is equipped. Corsetti fits an OME damper to every 60 it builds, lifted or not.
repairs.tools: Jacks and stands · breaker bar · ARB-111 (medium load) or equivalent kit · grease gun

parts.name: Old Man Emu 60 Series suspension kit, FJ60/FJ62 (OME60KIT)

repairs.title: Fix power-steering leaks
repairs.symptoms: Fluid on the driver's-side axle and spring, low fluid, or a groaning pump.
repairs.fix: Clean everything and find the source: the steering box, the pump or a hose. Replace hoses first, since they're cheapest. A leaking box needs resealing or a rebuilt unit, after which you refill and bleed by turning lock to lock with the engine running.
repairs.tools: Line wrenches · Pitman arm puller (box removal) · power-steering fluid · drain pan

parts.name: Power steering pump rebuild kit, 8/1987+ FJ62 (ST30030)
Power steering pump, OEM Toyota, 1988–1990 FJ62 (ST60090)
Steering box adjuster plug seal, FJ60/FJ62 (ST19002)

repairs.title: Rust repair at the rear wheel wells
repairs.symptoms: Bubbling at the rear wheel arches, a patched-feeling inner well, or a mud flap that sits unevenly.
repairs.fix: Fold the rear seat and peel back the inner wheel-well cover to see the inside. Cut out rust to clean metal, weld in patch panels, seam-seal and protect the area. Corsetti calls inner wheel-well rust common and relatively easy to repair; frame-rail rust is a different matter and needs professional assessment.
repairs.tools: Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · seam sealer · rust converter and cavity wax

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: On a stock FJ62, one IH8MUD member runs 33x9.50s with no problems. 33x10.50 might fit, but 33x12.50s won't without a lift. Many owners choose 31x10.50R15, which looks right at stock height or with about 2.5 inches of lift, though some shops won't mount it on the stock 15x6 wheel.

The FJ62 has fuel injection, 155 hp, an automatic and a plusher cabin, so it's easier to drive every day. The [[land-cruiser/fj60|FJ60]] has the carbureted 2F, a four-speed manual and round headlights. Hagerty calls the FJ60 the more collectible of the two.

faq.q: Is the 3F-E the same engine as an early 80 Series?
faq.a: Yes. IH8MUD members note the 3F-E was used only in the FJ62 and the 1991–92 [[land-cruiser/80-series|FJ80]], so parts and knowledge carry across.

faq.q: Can I convert it to a manual?
faq.a: Yes, with an H55F five-speed, but it's a big job. You'll need a manual bellhousing, flywheel, clutch, pedal and hydraulics, crossmember and floor modifications, shift linkage, driveshaft changes and some wiring.
Corsetti lists 3,500 lb, the same as the FJ60.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: Corsetti lists 12 mpg city and 19 highway with a 23.8-gallon tank. Real-world numbers on bigger tires are lower.

faq.q: Is a little oil leak normal?
faq.a: On a truck this age, mostly yes. As one IH8MUD member put it, 'any '88 Cruiser is going to leak some oil, from somewhere.' Check the pan bolts and valve cover gasket before assuming it's the rear main seal.
The common setup is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit for 4/1985–1/1990 trucks, in light, medium or heavy load ratings, with greaseable shackles and a steering damper.
The Japanese-market version introduced in 1987 with the 3F-E. Wikipedia says it let the Land Cruiser be sold in Japan as a passenger vehicle rather than a commercial one.
Hagerty's wagon-values piece put the median quote for 60 Series trucks at $18,500, with the FJ60 the more collectible. Restomod FJ62s from specialist shops sell for far more.

baseline_service.intro: An FJ62 is now 35+ years old, so treat every fluid and rubber part as suspect. The good news is that it's simple: a pushrod six with no timing belt, one automatic, a gear-driven part-time transfer case and two greased-knuckle solid axles. The specs below come from Toyota publications compiled on IH8MUD.

items.spec: 3F-E: 7.8 L with filter change (Toyota publications via IH8MUD); IH8MUD owners quote 8.2 qt as the official figure · viscosity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Fill to the dipstick, not a number: the oil cooler holds some oil, and IH8MUD owners report 7–8.5 qt depending on how fully it drained. Pre-filling the filter helps.
Check the rubber intake hose for cracks while the lid is off; an air leak after the meter can upset the EFI.

items.spec: Plugs, wires, cap, rotor and PCV valve
items.interval: Now, then per the owner's manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: The F-series is an OHV engine (Wikipedia), so there is no timing belt to budget for. IH8MUD members start rough-idle hunts with a tune-up and a full set of vacuum hoses.

items.spec: Ethylene-glycol coolant · 16.5 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.interval: Flush now, then every 2 years [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Replace any hose that is hard or swollen, and check the upper thermostat housing and radiator for old repairs; overheating history matters on a big iron six.

items.spec: Dexron II ATF · 5 L drain-and-refill, 15 L dry fill (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: A drain-and-refill only changes about a third of the fluid, so do two or three a few hundred miles apart on unknown fluid rather than a pressure flush. Drop the pan and change the strainer once.

items.spec: API GL-4 or GL-5, SAE 90 · 2.1 L with the A440F (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Fill until it runs out of the fill hole, and remove the fill plug before the drain plug.

items.spec: API GL-5 hypoid gear oil, SAE 80W-90 · 3.0 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Milky oil means water got in through the breather or seals, common after deep crossings.

items.spec: API GL-5 hypoid gear oil, SAE 80W-90 · 2.5 L; LSD oil if fitted with a limited-slip (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Check the pinion seal and axle-end seals for weeps while you're under there.

items.spec: Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.note: Grease weeping from the knuckle wipers is the classic 60-series leak (Corsetti). If the knuckle grease is runny, gear oil is getting past the inner axle seal.

items.spec: Dexron or Dexron II ATF · 0.81 L total, 0.39 L reservoir only (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.note: Check the box, pump and hoses for weeps at the same time; leaks often show on the driver's-side axle and spring.

parts.name: Steering box adjuster plug seal, FJ60/FJ62 (ST19002)

items.spec: DOT 3 / SAE J1703 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.interval: Flush now, then every 2 years [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Old fluid in a 30-year-old system means sticky calipers and corroded lines; inspect the hard lines while bleeding.

parts.name: Brake master cylinder rebuild kit, 8/1987–1/1990 FJ62 (BMK60160KOEM)

items.spec: Driveshafts: lithium-base NLGI-2 · steering link ends: moly lithium NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD)
items.note: Grease the U-joints and slip yokes. Greaseable shackles and pins, like those in OME kits, need regular grease too.

items.interval: Replace now if there's no record
items.note: An old filter starves the EFI and can mimic a rough-idle or vacuum problem.
